messages:
Jordan (Support): hey team, escalating a customer report — they got sustained 429s and their burst credits dropped to 0 even though the spike was only ~90s long. customer id: acct_8Xh2. they say requests were mostly short chat completions (avg 40 tokens) but burst came from a synchronous fan-out job. logs attached below. any quick mitigations?

Maya (Customer): pinging in — we run a scheduled sync that fan-outs 1200 small requests in a tight loop. historically we were fine, but yesterday at ~14:03 UTC most started failing with 429 and then continued failing for ~3m. we saw header: "x-redwood-burst-credits: 0" in errors. is smoothing supposed to handle this?

Jordan (Support): here's an anonymized error payload we got from their request logs: ```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "burst credits exhausted",
  "headers": {
    "x-redwood-burst-credits": "0",
    "x-redwood-burst-regen-seconds": "45",
    "x-request-id": "req_01F8..."
  }
}```

Priya (SRE): thanks. couple quick asks: (1) can you share the per-second request histogram for the window (14:02:30-14:06:00)? (2) any client retries/backoff config? smoothing only helps if traffic is somewhat continuous — huge sync fanouts can still deplete credits. also forwarding ops-bot traces.

Jordan (Support): per-customer time series from our metric store (1s buckets) for that window included in the paste: ```
2025-11-12T14:02:30Z  ->  10 rps
2025-11-12T14:02:40Z  ->  350 rps
2025-11-12T14:02:41Z  ->  420 rps
2025-11-12T14:02:42Z  ->  480 rps
2025-11-12T14:02:43Z  -> 500 rps
2025-11-12T14:03:30Z  -> 40 rps
```
so spike was ~20s of very high concurrent requests. client currently does immediate retry on 429 with fixed 1s delay (no jitter).

Luca (Backend): that explains it. quick summary of relevant bits: burst credits are a short-lived reserve tied to an account; credits regen at a fixed rate and have a hard cap. smoothing policy will spread sudden bursts by allowing brief oversubscription but only when the moving-window utilization hasn't already been high. a synchronous fan-out that pushes hundreds of concurrent requests in a few seconds can exhaust both the instant concurrency allowance and the burst credits.

Luca (Backend): repro tips: you can reproduce with a simple script that fire-and-forgets N parallel requests. example:```bash
for i in $(seq 1 500); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rw-small-1","input":"hi"}' &
done
wait
```
this floods the account in <10s and should show x-redwood-burst-credits drop to 0 and 429s start.

Priya (SRE): immediate mitigations for the customer: (A) add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s (we recommend base 250ms, multiplier 2, jitter 0.5-1.0), (B) change their fan-out to windowed concurrency (limit parallelism to ~20-50 depending on plan) or stagger starts, (C) we can temporarily bump their burst window / credits on the backend for 1 hour while they change the job — needs ops approval.

Jordan (Support): customer requested a temporary bump and asked whether enabling smoothing would have prevented this. 

Luca (Backend): smoothing helps for gradual increases and for clients that do many small requests spread over a few seconds. it does not magically absorb an atomic spike that is 500x baseline for 10s. implementation detail: smoothing uses a 30s EWMA and an internal per-account concurrency token bucket. regen rate is tuned per plan; we can tune for this account but that's a policy change.

ops-bot: runbook action created #RB-935: "support: customer acct_8Xh2 temporary burst bump request" assigned to @Priya (SRE).

Priya (SRE): I'll do a one-hour credits bump if legal says ok; need customer confirmation they will throttle after. Jordan — can you get a calendar ETA on their fix? also share the job config (how they fan-out).

Maya (Customer): thanks — we can gate the job to 40 parallel workers and add jitter. rolling out the change now, 10min ETA. please do the temporary bump so we don't break production while we deploy.

Jordan (Support): noted. action items: 1) Priya to approve + apply 1h temporary credits increase (ops). 2) Customer to throttle to 40 concurrency + add jitter. 3) Follow-up in 1h to verify no further 429s. I'll attach the exact job snippet to the ticket. :thumbsup:

Priya (SRE): applied temporary bump (ops note: +300 burst credits, expires in 1h). monitor link: https://console.redwood.ai/accounts/acct_8Xh2/metrics?range=1h :eyes:

Jordan (Support): monitoring shows successful steady state after throttling rollout. will keep ticket open until bump expires. thanks everyone.

Maya (Customer): confirmed no more 429s after change. appreciate the fast help.

Jordan (Support): closing loop — will add a short KB article: "How to avoid burst-credit exhaustion during synchronous fan-outs" with recommended client patterns, cURL repro, and ops escalation steps.
